question.text: A mixture of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Ca</mi><msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>OH</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of sodium sulphate was dissolved in water and the volume was made up to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>mL</mi><mo>.</mo></math> What is the mass of calcium sulphate formed and the concentration of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>OH</mi><mo>-</mo></msup></math> in resulting solution, respectively? (Molar mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Ca</mi><msub><mfenced separators="|"><mi>OH</mi></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msub><mi>Na</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CaSO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> are <math><mn>74</mn><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><mn>143</mn><mi> </mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>136</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mtext> </mtext><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></math> respectively; <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi>sp</mi></msub></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Ca</mi><msub><mfenced separators="|"><mi>OH</mi></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msub><mo> </mo><mi>is</mi><mtext> </mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>.5</mo><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
Mass of CaSO4=14×1361000=1.9 g

CaSO4=14×1361000=1.9 g
